# Credo

> Credo is an open source TypeScript framework for verifiable credentials. It is used to build issuers, verifiers, wallets and mediators that exchange SD-JWT VC, mdoc, W3C and AnonCreds credentials over OpenID4VC and DIDComm, on Node.js and React Native.

These docs are for Credo 0.7 (stable). Every page is available as Markdown by adding `.md` to its URL. All pages in one file: https://credo.js.org/llms-full.txt

## Docs

- [Credo documentation](https://credo.js.org/guides.md): Build issuers, verifiers, wallets and mediators for verifiable credentials with Credo, an open source TypeScript framework.
- [Getting started](https://credo.js.org/guides/getting-started.md): What you need to build with Credo, and the order to read the getting started pages in.
- [Installation](https://credo.js.org/guides/getting-started/installation.md): Set up a Node.js or React Native (Expo) project and install Credo with its storage and key management packages.
- [Your first agent](https://credo.js.org/guides/getting-started/first-agent.md): Create, initialize and shut down a minimal Credo agent that stores records with Drizzle in SQLite and keys in Askar, and creates a did:key.
- [Example setups](https://credo.js.org/guides/getting-started/example-setups.md): Complete Credo agent configurations for a mobile wallet, an issuer and verifier service, a multi-tenant service, a DIDComm mediator and tests.
- [AI coding agents](https://credo.js.org/guides/getting-started/ai-agents.md): Give Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other AI tools the Credo docs as Markdown.
- [Concepts](https://credo.js.org/guides/concepts.md): Background on verifiable credentials, Credo agents and modules, DIDs and DIDComm, and the platforms Credo runs on.
- [Verifiable credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/concepts/verifiable-credentials.md): Issuers, holders and verifiers, credentials and presentations, and how exchange protocols, credential formats, key binding, selective disclosure, status and trust fit together in Credo.
- [Agents and modules](https://credo.js.org/guides/concepts/agents.md): What a Credo agent is, how modules add functionality to it, and how agent contexts and tenants keep data apart.
- [DIDs and DIDComm](https://credo.js.org/guides/concepts/did-and-didcomm.md): What decentralized identifiers and DID documents are, and how DIDComm uses them for messaging between agents.
- [Platforms](https://credo.js.org/guides/concepts/platform-and-environment.md): The platforms Credo supports, Node.js and React Native, how its packages are published, and which runtimes aren't supported.
- [Agent configuration](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup.md): The options of the Credo Agent class, the modules every agent has, and how to start, stop and update an agent.
- [Storage](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/storage.md): Compare Askar and Drizzle, the two storage modules for a Credo agent, and pick the one that fits your platform and deployment.
- [Askar](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/storage/askar.md): Configure Askar for encrypted storage and key management in a Credo agent, on SQLite or PostgreSQL, in Node.js and React Native.
- [Drizzle](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/storage/drizzle.md): Store Credo records in PostgreSQL or SQLite tables with Drizzle ORM, run the migrations, and move an existing Askar agent to Drizzle.
- [Key management](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/key-management.md): Choose and configure the key management backends of a Credo agent (Askar, Node.js, hardware-backed keys on React Native, or your own), and use agent.kms to create keys and sign.
- [Caching](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/caching.md): Choose and configure the cache a Credo agent uses for resolved DID documents, ledger objects and certificate revocation lists.
- [Multi-tenancy](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/multi-tenancy.md): Run many isolated tenants in one Credo agent with the tenants module, choose how their data is stored, and manage tenant sessions.
- [Logging](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/logging.md): Log what a Credo agent does with the built-in ConsoleLogger or your own logger, and choose the log level.
- [Protocols](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols.md): How OpenID4VC, DIDComm and the ISO mdoc protocols differ, which credential formats each one carries, and which one to use.
- [OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc.md): Issue, receive and verify credentials over HTTPS with OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP, using the @credo-ts/openid4vc module.
- [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md): Run an OpenID4VCI issuer with Credo, define credential configurations, create credentials for incoming requests and create credential offers.
- [Receiving credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/receive.md): Receive credentials with OpenID4VCI in a Credo wallet on Node.js or React Native, bind them to the wallet's keys and store them.
- [Issuance authorization and wallet security](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md): Choose an OpenID4VCI authorization flow, use Credo's authorization server, a chained or an external one, presentation during issuance, PKCE, DPoP, and wallet and key attestations.
- [Verifying credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md): Request and verify credential presentations with OpenID4VP and DCQL from a Credo verifier on Node.js.
- [Presenting credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/present.md): Present stored credentials to a verifier with OpenID4VP from a Credo wallet on Node.js or React Native, with DCQL or Presentation Exchange.
- [SD-JWT VC with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md): Issue, receive and verify SD-JWT VCs over OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP with Credo, including selective disclosure with DCQL and transaction data.
- [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md): Issue, receive and verify ISO 18013-5 mdocs, such as mobile driving licences, over OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP with Credo.
- [W3C VCs with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/w3c.md): Issue, receive and verify W3C Verifiable Credentials over OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP with Credo, as VCDM 1.1 JWTs or VCDM 2.0 SD-JWTs.
- [ISO mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc.md): How the ISO/IEC 18013-5 and 18013-7 presentation protocols for mdocs work, how they differ from OpenID4VP, and what Credo does for proximity and the Digital Credentials API.
- [Proximity (ISO 18013-5)](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc/proximity.md): Present mdocs in person over BLE after a QR code or NFC engagement from a React Native wallet with expo-mdoc-data-transfer and Credo, and verify the device response in a reader.
- [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md): How the W3C Digital Credentials API passes credential requests from a website to a wallet, the two protocols Credo supports over it (OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-7 Annex C), platform support, and which protocols and options to choose.
- [Building a verifier](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/verifier.md): Request credentials from a website with the W3C Digital Credentials API. A Credo backend creates OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-7 Annex C requests and verifies the response, and the web page calls the API in the browser.
- [Building a wallet](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/wallet.md): Answer W3C Digital Credentials API requests from websites in a React Native wallet with @animo-id/expo-digital-credentials-api and Credo. Register credentials with the operating system, share the store with the iOS extension, and answer OpenID4VP and org-iso-mdoc requests.
- [DIDComm](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm.md): Set up DIDComm messaging in Credo with the DidCommModule, choose protocols and transports, and listen for state changes.
- [Connections](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/connections.md): Create and accept out-of-band invitations, connect agents with DID Exchange, reuse connections and track connection state in Credo.
- [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/issue-credential.md): Issue credentials over DIDComm with the Issue Credential v2 protocol, register credential formats and handle offers, requests and auto-accept.
- [Requesting proofs](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/present-proof.md): Request and verify presentations over DIDComm with the Present Proof v2 protocol, using AnonCreds or DIF Presentation Exchange.
- [Mediation](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/mediation.md): Run a DIDComm mediator with Credo and connect mobile agents to it, with message pickup, live delivery and keylist updates.
- [Messaging and other protocols](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/messaging.md): Send basic messages over a DIDComm connection, and add the action menu, question answer and DIDComm RPC protocols to a Credo agent.
- [AnonCreds with DIDComm](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/anoncreds.md): Issue AnonCreds credentials and request proofs with predicates over DIDComm, and handle revocation.
- [W3C VCs with DIDComm](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/w3c.md): Issue W3C Verifiable Credentials over DIDComm as JSON-LD, Data Integrity or VCDM 2.0 SD-JWT credentials, and present them with DIF Presentation Exchange.
- [Credential formats](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats.md): The credential formats Credo supports, how they compare, and which one to use.
- [SD-JWT VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/sd-jwt-vc.md): Sign, store, present and verify IETF SD-JWT VCs with agent.sdJwtVc, independent of the exchange protocol.
- [mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/mdoc.md): Sign, store, present and verify ISO 18013-5 mdocs, such as the mobile driving licence, with agent.mdoc.
- [W3C Verifiable Credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/w3c-vc.md): Sign, store, present and verify W3C Verifiable Credentials (data model 1.1 and 2.0) as JWT, SD-JWT, JSON-LD or Data Integrity.
- [AnonCreds](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/anoncreds.md): Set up AnonCreds in Credo with a registry, register schemas, credential definitions and revocation registries, and manage link secrets and stored credentials.
- [Status lists](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/status-lists.md): Revoke and suspend SD-JWT VCs and mdocs with IETF Token Status Lists, using agent.tokenStatusList.
- [DIDs](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust.md): Choose between X.509 certificates and DIDs, pick a DID method, and create, resolve and import DIDs with agent.dids.
- [X.509 certificates](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/x509.md): Create self-signed and CA-issued X.509 certificates and certificate signing requests with agent.x509, parse certificates, validate chains and check revocation.
- [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md): How Credo decides whether to trust the issuer of a credential or the signer of a request, what it does by default, and how to configure trust with getTrustedIssuersForVerification and trusted X.509 certificates.
- [cheqd](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/cheqd.md): Create, update and deactivate did:cheqd DIDs, publish DID-linked resources, and use cheqd as an AnonCreds registry with @credo-ts/cheqd.
- [Indy VDR](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/indy-vdr.md): Connect to Hyperledger Indy networks with @credo-ts/indy-vdr to resolve did:indy and did:sov, register did:indy DIDs with an endorser, and use Indy as an AnonCreds registry.
- [Hedera](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/hedera.md): Create, update, deactivate and resolve did:hedera DIDs, and use Hedera as an AnonCreds registry with @credo-ts/hedera.
- [did:webvh](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/webvh.md): Create, update and resolve did:webvh DIDs with @credo-ts/webvh, host the DID log, and use did:webvh as an AnonCreds registry.
- [Supported standards](https://credo.js.org/guides/supported-standards.md): The exchange protocols, credential formats, DID methods and platforms Credo supports.
- [Updating Credo](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating.md): How Credo versions work, the steps to update an agent to a new version, and the migration guide for each version.
- [Updating from 0.6 to 0.7](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/versions/0.6-to-0.7.md): Dependency updates, breaking changes and deprecations when you update Credo from 0.6 to 0.7.
- [Migrating from Credo 0.5.x to 0.6.x](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/versions/0.5-to-0.6.md)
- [updating/versions/0.4-to-0.5](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/versions/0.4-to-0.5.md)
- [updating/versions/0.3-to-0.4](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/versions/0.3-to-0.4.md)
- [updating/versions/0.2-to-0.3](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/versions/0.2-to-0.3.md)
- [updating/versions/0.1-to-0.2](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/versions/0.1-to-0.2.md)
- [updating/update-assistant](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/update-assistant.md)
- [updating/update-indy-sdk-to-askar](https://credo.js.org/guides/updating/update-indy-sdk-to-askar.md)
- [Ecosystem](https://credo.js.org/guides/ecosystem.md): The Credo repositories, the libraries Credo builds on, and open source projects built with Credo.
- [Extensions](https://credo.js.org/guides/extensions.md): The Credo extension packages from credo-ts-ext, what each one does, and which Credo version they work with.
- [REST API](https://credo.js.org/guides/extensions/rest.md): Run a Credo 0.5 agent behind a REST API with the @credo-ts/rest CLI.
- [React hooks](https://credo.js.org/guides/extensions/react-hooks.md): Read the connections, credentials and proofs of a Credo 0.5 agent in React with @credo-ts/react-hooks.
- [Redux store](https://credo.js.org/guides/extensions/redux-store.md): Keep the state of a Credo 0.5 agent in a Redux Toolkit store with @credo-ts/redux-store.
- [Push notifications](https://credo.js.org/guides/extensions/push-notifications.md): Share an APNs or Firebase push notification token with another agent over DIDComm, with @credo-ts/push-notifications for Credo 0.5.
